newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sugar beet harvesting gets underway.
newsitem.headline: French sugar beet harvesting gets underway.

text.p: Sugar beet harvesting got under way this week in France with at least one of the country's 45 processing factories starting operations, sugar producers said on Wednesday.
"At least one processing plant started operations this week and a few more are due to start from September 26 onwards," a spokeswoman for the French sugar manufacturers association SNFS told Reuters.
The harvest started around the same time last year.
While scattered rain did not hamper the start of harvesting, cool temperatures have been limiting beet growth, an analyst for the French beet planters federation (CGB) said.
But planters may have firmer crop data later this week following the release of their fifth and last test, he said

The fourth and last beet test carried out by the French sugar manufacturers on September 9 and released on September 13 showed sugar weight per hectare fell to 9.382 tonnes from 9.951 tonnes last year.
This was a fall of 10.9 percent from the five-year average of 10.523 tonnes.
After the test French sugar intervention board FIRS said it was maintaining its estimate of a 1996/97 beet sugar output of 3.9 million tonnes against 4.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
